key_insight: Long tasks do not necessarily require long model contexts. Frequent context compaction preserves little-to-no-loss task accuracy across a broad range of long-input and long-horizon tasks while keeping contexts short.
problem_solved: As context grows, generating later tokens becomes more expensive—up to 7× costlier than earlier tokens on frontier open-weight models. The paper investigates whether models can avoid this overhead without sacrificing task performance.
method: Frequently compact accumulated context to maintain a shorter working context.
Evaluate task accuracy across a broad range of long-input and long-horizon tasks.
Test long-horizon software engineering with at most one action per context, finding that performance does not collapse.
impact: Context compaction offers practitioners a way to reduce growing inference costs without necessarily compromising accuracy. The findings suggest that effective context management can matter more than retaining an entire interaction history.
visual_elements: Token-cost chart highlighting the reported disparity of up to 7× between earlier and later tokens.
Before-and-after diagram showing a growing interaction history compacted into a short working context.
Conceptual accuracy comparison showing similar performance with long versus frequently compacted contexts.
Software-engineering workflow illustrating one action per context across a long task.
paper_authors: Peter Belcak, Saurav Muralidharan, Jindong Jiang, Yonggan Fu, Wonmin Byeon
